concerns.text: Phase 2 states: “Zero‑impute only when the source explicitly states class absent; otherwise drop row.” Zero‑imputed values are then subjected to z‑score standardization (Phase 2.5). Imputing a literal zero before standardization forces those absent‑metabolite observations to be transformed to the column mean after z‑scoring, conflating biological absence with average concentration. This can bias correlation and regression estimates and undermines the validity of the downstream validation (e.g., significance of negative correlations). A more appropriate approach would either (a) treat documented absence as a separate binary indicator (as already allowed by the optional `absence_indicator` field) and exclude those rows from the standardization, or (b) perform imputation after standardization using a method that respects the distribution (e.g., mean‑imputation on the standardized scale).
